GPU memory bandwidth is the rate at which data can be read from or written to the GPU's video memory (VRAM), typically measured in gigabytes per second (GB/s). It is a critical performance metric because modern GPUs are massively parallel processors that can perform trillions of floating-point operations per second, and they need a constant supply of data to keep those compute units busy. If the memory bandwidth is insufficient, the GPU will stall waiting for data, leaving compute resources idle—a condition known as being "memory-bound." This is especially important for workloads like deep learning, where training a neural network involves repeatedly moving large weight matrices and activation tensors between compute cores and memory, or for high-resolution gaming, where the GPU must stream textures and geometry data at 60+ frames per second.
